---
title: "Where a Gamma prior exists"
subtitle: "Catalog C-06"
description: "The (mu_K, sigma^2) plane at J units: below the profile bound no Gamma prior can meet a count target, above the support ceiling no count can; drag a target and TSMM re-solves at once."
toc: false
---

Not every count target has a Gamma hyperprior. At J units, a target mean mu_K for K_J (the
number of clusters) allows only a band of variances. Mixing over alpha always adds variance,
so no Gamma prior can be tighter than the point mass alpha* whose mean count is mu_K. That is
the profile bound v_J(alpha*), the red curve. Above the grey curve no count on 1..J has the
variance at all: the curve is the count that puts all its mass on 1 and J.

```{=html}
<div id="w-feas" class="dpx-host column-page"></div>
<script src="../../js/vendor/d3.min.js"></script>
<script src="../../js/vendor/plot.min.js"></script>
<script src="../../js/bundles/feasibility-map.js"></script>
<script>
  (function () {
    var q = new URLSearchParams(location.search), spec = {};
    ["J", "mu", "var"].forEach(function (k) { var v = q.get(k); if (v !== null && v !== "" && isFinite(+v)) spec[k] = +v; });
    if (q.get("preset")) spec.preset = q.get("preset");
    window.__dpxFeas = DPX["feasibility-map"].mountWidget(document.getElementById("w-feas"), spec);
  })();
</script>
```

- **The [3, 10] example at J = 100.** "Between 3 and 10 clusters with 80% probability" is the
  target (6.5, 7.46), inside the band: Gamma(6.82, 4.82). The same interval at 95% is
  (6.5, 3.19), below the red curve, which passes 4.52 at mu_K = 6.5 (alpha* = 1.386). No
  Gamma prior has that little variance, so TSMM reports "no solution" rather than a poor fit.
- **The bound moves little with J.** At mu_K = 6.5 the smallest variance is 4.20 at J = 50,
  4.52 at J = 100 and 4.91 at J = 500; the ceiling grows with J.
- **Near the red curve the prior is almost a point mass.** Within about .002 of the curve
  the solution has CV(alpha) < .01 (the gold edge). TSMM still finds that exact solution, with
  a large shape a, and labels it nearly a point mass.
- **Near the grey curve** the solution runs to a and b near zero. TSMM converges up to about
  95% of the ceiling; closer than that, b falls below 10^-17 and Newton stops without
  converging. Such targets say "anything from one cluster to J clusters", which is rarely meant.
  The ceiling itself is reached only by a count split between 1 and J, never by a Gamma prior.

The same check runs inside [the calibrator](calibrator.qmd) and [the elicitation form](elicitation.qmd),
which also name the widest probability or smallest VIF that would work.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
Curves from dp-core `profileBound` (bisection for alpha*, then v_J(alpha*)); fits from
`tsmmFit`. The bound for [3, 10] at 95% matches an independent R computation (uniroot on the
conditional mean, verification/golden/tsmm_fits.csv) to 1e-9; see [the parity page](tsmm-parity.qmd).
:::

(for example `?preset=i95` or `?J=500&mu=5&var=10`).
